findings: The existing single-run analyzer and new tool produce identical interval summaries for the same Actions snapshot.

The new tool additionally binds plan digest, selected targets, run/base/head identity, artifact digest/file list, and receipt-presence semantics; the existing single-run output does not provide those associations.
The repeated-step analyzer requires multiple runs, so its distinct multi-run use case remains uncovered by this one-run comparison.
replacement_or_retirement: No existing tool is shown to cover all of its valuable uses. Keep the timeline tool for interval-only analysis and the repeated-step analyzer for multi-run history; retain this optional specialist for plan/artifact/receipt attribution.
uncertainty_and_limits: The follow-up route trial measured local wall time, child CPU and input/output bytes for three fresh CLI samples on one machine; these observations are task-specific and do not establish general performance or resource cost.
No analyst-time, token, hosted-runner billable-minute, cash-cost, savings, or waste comparison was performed.
The source snapshot and artifact inventory are caller-supplied and unauthenticated by this tool; neither the functional comparison nor the route trial certifies CI or target results.

follow_up_route_trial.same_task: PR #264 run 40064357026, same plan, Actions snapshot and artifact inventory
follow_up_route_trial.outcome: Attribution-only met the frozen job-level plan/artifact/receipt contract. Timeline-only met an interval-only contract but not the full attribution contract. The two-tool counterfactual added no required fact for this task and the adaptive router selected attribution alone.
follow_up_route_trial.interpretation_limit: One local task and three subprocess samples only. No general runtime, analyst-time, token, hosted-runner billing, cash-cost, savings, waste or reliability claim.
